questions.stem: A buyer and a seller both believed the sale included a vacant parcel across the road. After signing, they learn the parcel was never part of the seller's property. The contract is most likely
choices: fully enforceable, because a mistake is never a defense to a signed contract
void or voidable, because both parties were mistaken about a material fact
voidable only by the seller, because the seller owned the property being sold
unenforceable under the Statute of Frauds, because the parcel was described in writing
questions.explanation: A mutual mistake about a material fact can make a contract void or voidable. A unilateral mistake, or a mistake about value or the law, usually isn't a defense, but here both parties shared the mistake.

questions.stem: A buyer promises to pay $400,000 and the seller promises to convey the house at closing. Classified by who is bound, this purchase contract is
choices: unilateral, because only the buyer has to come up with money
implied, because it is created by the parties' conduct
bilateral
voidable by either party until closing
questions.explanation: A bilateral contract is a promise for a promise, so both parties are obligated. A unilateral contract is a promise for an act (like an option), where only one party is bound.

questions.stem: A buyer discovers the seller lied about a material fact to get the buyer to sign. The buyer wants to cancel the contract and get the earnest money deposit back. Which remedy fits?
choices: Rescission
Specific performance
Liquidated damages
Acceptance of breach
questions.explanation: Rescission cancels the contract and puts the parties back where they started, with deposits returned; it's the typical remedy for a contract induced by fraud or mutual mistake. Specific performance would force the sale to go through, the opposite of what the buyer wants.

questions.stem: A tenant has a one-year lease with fixed start and end dates. Four months in, the owner sells the building. What happens to the lease?
choices: It ends automatically when the deed is recorded
The new owner takes title subject to the existing lease
It converts to a tenancy at will that either party can end
It becomes a periodic tenancy that the new owner can end on notice
questions.explanation: A sale doesn't end an estate for years; the buyer takes the property subject to existing leases. The tenant keeps possession through the lease's end date.

questions.stem: A tenant signs a lease that gives her the right, but not the obligation, to buy the home at a set price during the term. This arrangement is a
choices: lease-purchase
graduated lease
ground lease
lease option
questions.explanation: A lease option is a lease plus an option to buy: the tenant may buy but isn't required to. In a lease-purchase, the tenant agrees to buy, so both sides are obligated to complete the sale.

questions.stem: An owner buys an NFIP flood insurance policy on his own; no loan is being made, increased, extended or renewed. When does coverage generally begin?
choices: Immediately, on the day the premium is paid
After the next FEMA flood map update
After a 30-day waiting period
Only once the home is placed in a special flood hazard area
questions.explanation: NFIP policies generally have a 30-day waiting period. The exception is a policy bought in connection with making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan, which doesn't apply here. Owners outside mapped high-risk zones can still buy flood coverage.

questions.stem: A listing broker receives a second offer on the seller's home while the seller is reviewing the first one. Which fiduciary duty requires the broker to tell the seller about it?
choices: Disclosure
Confidentiality
Obedience
Accounting
questions.explanation: The duty of disclosure requires the broker to tell the client everything material, including other offers. Confidentiality works the other way: it protects the client's private information from others.

questions.stem: A buyer's broker recommends a roofing contractor to repair the roof after closing. The contractor pays the broker a fee for every client referred. What is the broker's obligation?
choices: Nothing, because the contractor is not a party to the real estate transaction
Disclose the fee in writing before the client relies on the recommendation
Mention the fee to the client verbally at any point before the closing appointment
Nothing, as long as the contractor's prices are in line with other local contractors
questions.explanation: A broker must disclose any personal interest, including a referral fee from a vendor they recommend, in writing before the client relies on it. A verbal mention, or a fair price, doesn't cure it; an undisclosed payment is a secret profit that violates the duty of loyalty.

questions.stem: Two competing brokers agree that one will take listings only on the west side of town and the other only on the east side. This antitrust violation is
choices: a tie-in arrangement
price fixing
a group boycott
market allocation
questions.explanation: Market allocation is competitors dividing up territory, customers, price ranges or property types. Price fixing concerns agreed rates, a group boycott targets a competitor, and a tie-in conditions one product on buying another.

questions.stem: A licensee paid entirely by commission wants to be treated as a statutory nonemployee for federal tax purposes. Besides being licensed and paid based on sales output, what else is required?
choices: A written agreement stating she won't be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes
At least two years of continuous affiliation with the same employing broker
An agreement that the employing broker will stop supervising her work
Proof that she pays for her own errors and omissions coverage
questions.explanation: The IRS treats a licensed agent as a statutory nonemployee when she is licensed, substantially all pay is based on sales output, and a written agreement says she won't be treated as an employee for federal tax purposes. License law still requires the employing broker to supervise her either way.

questions.stem: In most states, which task may a broker's unlicensed assistant perform?
choices: Hold an open house alone on a weekend
Schedule showing appointments for the broker
Discuss price and terms with a buyer who calls
Show a listing to a buyer when the broker is busy
questions.explanation: Unlicensed assistants may do clerical and administrative work such as scheduling, data entry and ordering reports. Showing property, negotiating, discussing terms and holding open houses alone are licensed activities.

questions.stem: A property manager sets aside a plan for replacing the roof and parking lot over the next several years. This is part of the
choices: operating budget
stabilized budget
capital budget
management agreement
questions.explanation: A capital budget plans for big-ticket replacements and improvements such as a roof, HVAC or parking lot. An operating budget projects the year's income and ordinary expenses; a stabilized budget averages expenses over several years.

questions.stem: A tenant is two months behind on rent. The landlord changes the locks while the tenant is at work. This is
choices: a lawful actual eviction, because the tenant breached the lease
generally illegal self-help; the landlord should use the court eviction process
a constructive eviction, which a landlord may use once rent is two months late
permitted if the landlord gives notice of the lock change the same day
questions.explanation: Actual eviction means removing the tenant through a court process after a breach. Self-help, such as changing locks or shutting off utilities, is generally illegal. Constructive eviction is a tenant's claim when the landlord makes the premises unusable, not a landlord remedy.

questions.stem: After several injuries, the owner of an apartment complex closes the swimming pool permanently. Which risk management strategy is this?
choices: Transfer
Control
Retain
Avoid
questions.explanation: Avoiding risk means removing the activity that creates it, such as closing the pool. Control reduces the chance or size of a loss (better lighting, handrails), transfer shifts it (insurance), and retain accepts it.

questions.stem: Under the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA), when does the act apply to a real estate transaction?
choices: Only when the parties have agreed to deal electronically, which can be shown by their conduct
In every transaction, whether or not the parties want electronic records
Only when the documents are notarized by an electronic notary
Only to commercial transactions, not consumer home sales
questions.explanation: UETA applies only when the parties agree to conduct the transaction electronically, and that agreement can be shown by conduct. Neither UETA nor E-SIGN forces anyone to use electronic records.
